heroSubtitle: Prohibitin-targeting peptidomimetic (FTPP) — a targeted-conjugate tool for adipose-tissue research
description: Adipotide (FTPP) is a synthetic peptidomimetic conjugate: a prohibitin-binding sequence coupled to a pro-apoptotic peptide. In rodent research models it has been used to study targeted apoptosis of the vasculature supporting white adipose tissue, making it a reference compound in targeted-peptide-conjugate research rather than a conventional signalling peptide.

faq.question: What is Adipotide?
faq.answer: Adipotide (FTPP) is a synthetic peptidomimetic that combines a prohibitin-binding sequence with a pro-apoptotic peptide. CAS 859216-15-2. It is a research reagent for laboratory use only.

faq.question: How is Adipotide different from a signalling peptide like GLP-1?
faq.answer: It is a targeted conjugate rather than a receptor agonist: its design targets prohibitin-expressing cells and delivers a pro-apoptotic peptide sequence, so research use centres on targeted delivery rather than metabolic signalling.
